title: The test ratchet must refuse a stale baseline (or derive it)
description: The ratchet let .test-baseline.json go stale: test-skills#14 added 18 cases and #15 raised the cap to 79, and neither advanced the baseline (still 60 while the suite is 79), so every later PR inherits phantom +19 growth and fails max_new_tests_per_pr. Fix by making the gate REFUSE a merge whose baseline is below the collected count on the base, or by deriving the baseline instead of hand-keeping it. Decided as DEC-209 on opum-doc dev (accepted, read 2026-10-19): REFUSE, and no run-time derivation; the stored baseline is the auditable reference and moves only through the Article XIII amendment path. Admitted for implementation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recorded baseline that does not match the base commit's measured test count fails the gate by name. It prints both numbers and the base SHA, and names the Article XIII amendment as the only way to move the baseline. A mismatch in either direction never passes.
There is no run-time derivation. The stored baseline stays the auditable reference.

Proved both ways: an equal count passes, and one count below and one above each fail by name with both numbers. A mutation that skips the comparison turns those two green, and the suite must catch it.
Review: Stage 1, or opum-doc's Opus review by ref if it touches a CI workflow file.

plan: 1. Read the gate path that consumes .test-baseline.json and max_new_tests_per_pr; find where the base commit count can be measured.

2. Implement REFUSE: a recorded baseline that does not match the base commit measured count fails by name, printing both numbers and the base SHA, naming Article XIII as the only way to move the baseline. No run-time derivation.
3. Tests both ways: equal passes; below fails; above fails. Add a mutation that skips the comparison and confirm the suite catches it.
4. Run the full suite, open the PR, and route review (Stage 1, or Opus by ref if a CI workflow file is touched).

FINDINGS
1. MAJOR skills/test-audit/scripts/tmx/gate.py:397 (`seen = len(measured & totals["ids"])`): scoping by this run's ids turns any PR that deletes or renames a test into a false refusal. Base 84, recorded 84, PR deletes 2 -> seen 82 != 84 -> stale_baseline. The baseline is read from the base (anti-tamper, `_from_base`, cli.py/gate.py:588-591), so the PR cannot repair it. Result: every test-reduction PR, which Article II and test-reduce encourage, is unmergeable. This follows the scoping in the ruling as relayed, so the DEC-209 owner should decide whether the scoping stays. A fix that fits the ruling: compare recorded against len(measured & (run ids | baseline test_ids)), or count a base id as missing only if the PR did not touch it. No test covers deletion, so the gap is invisible; name it as a coverage gap.
2. MAJOR gate.py:150-151 (`ids = _collected_ids(proc.stdout); return (True, ids) if ids else (True, None)`): proc.returncode is ignored. A suite with SOME collection errors (one broken file, others fine) still prints ids, so it counts as measured with a partial count. That conflicts with "a suite that exists but cannot be collected FAILS by name". It reports as stale_baseline, which is misleading. It can also false-pass if the recorded baseline equals the partial count, or the broken file's ids are absent from this run. Fix: treat returncode not in (0,) with any "error" in the output as (True, None). The new unmeasurable test (tests/test_gate.py:296-309) covers only the all-broken case, where ids are empty, so a partial-collection mutation survives.
3. MINOR gate.py:379: the whole check is gated on `baseline and max_new_tests_per_pr is not None and base`. A policy without max_new_tests_per_pr, or a run without junit, is never checked, and the skip is silent. Add info["baseline_measured"]="skipped" or document it in the SKILL.md/ci-snippet prose, which currently reads as unconditional.
4. MINOR gate.py:127-155: tarfile.TarError (a filter="data" FilterError) is not caught; only TimeoutExpired and OSError are. It would crash rather than report baseline_unmeasured. It fails closed, so not a false-pass. Also, `git archive` honours export-ignore in the base's .gitattributes, so an excluded tests dir reads as not-a-pytest-project and silently skips.
5. MINOR gate.py:98-99: a parametrize id containing "::" is split wrongly by the node-id normalisation. A `_has_python_tests` result of False, or test_roots naming a missing dir, also skips silently.
6. MINOR gate.py:400-405: the message says "the normal amendment path (Article XIII)" but never says it is the ONLY way to move the baseline (AC0 wording). Test line 292 asserts only "Article XIII" and "amendment".
7. MINOR tests/test_gate.py:269-277: the pass test never asserts res["passed"] is True. It checks only the absence of the rule and baseline_measured == 1.
8. MINOR coverage gaps (not asking for new tests): (a) no case distinguishes scoped from unscoped counting, so a mutation to `seen = len(measured)` survives; (b) the `--python` flag and the cli main() path with --base are not exercised for the new rule (the modified loosen-gate test goes through the CLI but only with an equal count); (c) deletion/rename, see 1.

MINOR gate.py:428 (`seen = len(measured & (totals["ids"] | baseline test_ids))`): the union can hide a stale baseline where the PR itself removes or renames base tests that the baseline does not list. Example: baseline says 79 with 79 ids, base really runs 84. A PR whose JUnit omits exactly those 5 unlisted tests gets seen == 79 and passes, although the base count is 84. This needs an exact coincidence, and the PR supplies the JUnit, so it is narrow. A PR that keeps all 84 is refused (84 != 79). It is not a false pass in the ordinary stale case, and it is the cost of closing round-1 major 1. Record it as a known limit. A new case is not allowed under 84, so I am not asking for one.
2. MINOR gate.py:231-240 (`_collected_ids`): a nested class `A::B::test` becomes `mod.A::B::test`. JUnit's classname is `mod.A.B`, so the ids never intersect. Result: undercount, so a false refusal (it fails closed) for suites with nested test classes. The "::"-in-parametrize fix is correct, because "[" in parts[0] stops the class split.
3. MINOR tests/test_gate.py (pass fixture): scope = baseline ids alone would also pass it, because test_slow is in neither the run nor the baseline. So that mutant survives. The run-ids-only mutant, the unscoped mutant and the compare-skip mutant do each turn something red.

R1-2 MAJOR (nonzero collection returncode treated as measured): FIXED. gate.py:312 returns (True, None) when returncode != 0. The partly broken fixture then yields baseline_unmeasured. R1-3 MINOR (silent skip): FIXED. info["baseline_measured"] is set to "skipped (needs --base, a JUnit report, a baseline and max_new_tests_per_pr)".
R1-4 MINOR (tarfile errors, export-ignore): FIXED. TarError, EOFError and ValueError return (True, None). Applicability now comes from `git ls-tree` on the base, so an export-ignore'd suite reads as unmeasured, not as absent.

LIMIT 1 (verdict finding 1, gate.py scope union): the union in the stale check can hide a stale baseline where a PR removes or renames base tests that the baseline does not list AND its JUnit omits exactly those ids. Example from the verdict: baseline says 79 with 79 ids while the base runs 84; a PR whose report omits exactly those 5 unlisted tests reads 79 and passes. It needs an exact coincidence and the PR supplies the JUnit, so it is narrow; a PR that keeps all 84 is refused. This is the cost of closing round-1 major 1 (a reduction no longer reading as stale), and it is the cheaper of the two failures.

LIMIT 2 (verdict finding 2, _collected_ids): a nested test class A::B::test normalises to mod.A::B::test while JUnit reports classname mod.A::B. The ids never intersect, so a suite with nested test classes undercounts and is falsely refused. It fails CLOSED, not open.
